sections.h2: How does selling a house in Mountlake Terrace work?
sections.html:
A Mountlake Terrace owner can list the house, sell it directly, or accept a cash offer from a buyer who takes it as-is. Each path ends with a deed, an excise tax affidavit, and a recording with Snohomish County.

Mountlake Terrace is a suburban city on the southern edge of Snohomish County, next to Shoreline and Lynnwood and about 13 miles north of downtown Seattle on Interstate 5. The Census Bureau estimates 25,430 residents as of July 1, 2025, packed into 4.06 square miles of land. The 2020 density was 5,248 people per square mile, and much of the housing dates to the city's postwar founding, covered below.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show about Mountlake Terrace homes?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau lists a median owner-occupied value of $667,300 and an owner-occupied rate of 56.9 percent for 2020 to 2024. Median gross rent is $2,004 and median household income is $107,687.

sections.h2: Why are so many Mountlake Terrace houses from the 1950s?
sections.html:
The city started as a planned veterans' suburb. Real estate developers bought a disused World War II landing field in 1949 and named the project Mountlake Terrace for its plateau setting, with views toward Lake Washington and Mount Rainier.

Construction on the first 250 homes began in June 1949. They used a simple two-bedroom plan of 20 by 30 feet, built in an assembly line, and the first ones were priced from $4,999. Developers added larger homes to the north and east in later years, and the early houses were renovated and expanded with Federal Housing Administration help. The community passed 5,000 residents within five years and incorporated on November 29, 1954. If you own one of those early houses, expect a buyer's inspector to look closely at additions, wiring, and plumbing, and expect questions about whether the remodels were permitted.

sections.h2: What are Mountlake Terrace's neighborhoods and boundaries?
sections.html:
The city planning map has six neighborhoods. The city sits on a plateau with elevations from 263 to 528 feet, and its edges follow Hall Creek and the Interurban Trail on the west, 212th Street Southwest on the north, and 39th Avenue West on the east.

  • Town Center: between 220th and 236th streets, with retailers, restaurants, and civic buildings near Veterans Memorial Park.
  • Cedar Terrace: east of the Town Center and Terrace Creek Park, mostly residential with apartments along Cedar Way.
  • Cascade View: the north side from Interstate 5 east to Brier, including the high school campus.
  • Gateway: a residential area south of the Town Center, with a commercial center at the I-5 and State Route 104 interchange.
  • Lake Ballinger and Melody Hill: the remaining two planning neighborhoods. Lake Ballinger is a 100-acre lake in the southwest that drains toward Lake Washington.

Name the neighborhood in your listing or cash offer request. It tells buyers which schools, roads, and transit stops apply.

sections.h2: How do commuters and employers shape Mountlake Terrace?
sections.html:
Most residents work elsewhere. In 2018 figures, only 3.2 percent of employed residents worked inside city limits, and 37.0 percent commuted to Seattle. The largest employer is Premera Blue Cross, with 2,446 employees in 2022.

Interstate 5 has interchanges at State Route 104 (244th Street Southwest), 236th Street Southwest, and 220th Street Southwest, and State Route 99 touches the western edge. The Mountlake Terrace transit station, which opened in 2009, has 890 parking stalls and has been served by Link light rail since the line to Lynnwood opened in August 2024. Community Transit runs local routes to Edmonds, Lynnwood, and Brier, and King County Metro serves the station from Shoreline, Lake Forest Park, and Kenmore. The Census Bureau puts the mean commute for city residents at 27.9 minutes, a number worth quoting in your listing.

sections.h2: Who provides schools and utilities in Mountlake Terrace?
sections.html:
Public schools belong to the Edmonds School District, which has five schools inside the city: one high school, one middle school, and three elementary schools. Mountlake Terrace High School opened in 1960, was rebuilt in 1991 on the same campus, and sits in the northeast corner of the city.

  • Electricity: Snohomish County Public Utility District.
  • Natural gas: Puget Sound Energy.
  • Water and sewer: Alderwood Water and Wastewater District.
  • Garbage, recycling, and yard waste: collected under city contract with Waste Management.

Tell buyers which providers serve the house so they can price the monthly bills.

sections.h2: What permit rules matter when you sell a Mountlake Terrace house?
sections.html:
Work done without a permit is the main risk. The city's permit FAQ says failing to get one before construction is a code violation that can bring fines, that you may have to obtain permits and pass inspection or restore the site, and that permit fees may be doubled as a penalty.

  • Window and siding installation, roofing, plumbing, electrical, and structural changes always need a permit.
  • Sheds over 80 square feet or over 6 feet high need one, and a garage turned into living space is a change of use that needs one.
  • Removing drywall and exposing framing needs one, even for a wall removal or remodel.
  • Like-for-like cabinet replacement, painting, and carpet do not.
  • Permits expire if work does not start and pass an inspection within 180 days.

The FAQ adds that an owner doing the work must live in the home, and that a contractor is required if you plan to rent or sell. Email the permit specialists at permitspecialist@mltwa.gov for a specific project, and check the posted counter hours before you visit.

sections.h2: What are the excise tax and recording steps in Snohomish County?
sections.html:
The Snohomish County Treasurer reviews the deed first, and the Auditor's Recording Division records it second. If excise tax is owed, the deed cannot be recorded until it is paid in full at the Treasurer's excise tax counter.

The counter is open Monday through Friday from 9 a.m. to 3 p.m., phone 425-388-3366, at 3000 Rockefeller Avenue in Everett. Recording is in the same building, open 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., phone 425-388-3483, and mail submissions need the exact recording fee. Recording fees depend on document type and page count.

The state tax is graduated at 1.1, 1.28, 2.75, and 3 percent by price slice, with the first breakpoint at $525,000 through December 31, 2026 and $551,000 from January 1, 2027. The local rate is added, and the tax is due on the date of sale, which the Department of Revenue treats as the notarization date. The seller disclosure statement in RCW 64.06.020 is due within five business days of mutual acceptance unless waived or exempt.

sections.h2: When does a cash offer make sense in Mountlake Terrace?
sections.html:
It makes sense when the house needs updating, when a probate or move is on a deadline, or when you want to avoid repairs a buyer's lender would require. Older houses with deferred updates are a typical fit.

Ask any buyer for proof of funds, a written closing date, and who pays the excise tax and title fees. Then compare the offer against a listing's net after excise tax, agent fees, repairs, and carrying costs. Request an offer on your Mountlake Terrace address to see the numbers side by side.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Mountlake Terrace house that has unpermitted work?
faqs.a: Yes, but expect it to come up. The city says work without a permit is a code violation, and you may have to obtain permits and pass inspection or return the site to its original condition. Ask the permit specialists about your case before listing, or sell to a buyer who takes the house as it stands.

faqs.q: Who records the deed for a Mountlake Terrace sale?
faqs.a: Snohomish County does. The Treasurer's Office reviews conveyance documents such as deeds for excise tax, and the Auditor's Recording Division records them after any tax is paid. Recording is at 3000 Rockefeller Avenue in Everett, phone 425-388-3483.

faqs.q: How much state excise tax would a $667,300 Mountlake Terrace sale owe?
faqs.a: The state portion is $7,596.44: $5,775 on the first $525,000 at 1.1 percent and $1,821.44 on the remaining $142,300 at 1.28 percent. The local excise tax is added, and sales closing after January 1, 2027 use higher breakpoints.

faqs.q: Which school district serves Mountlake Terrace?
faqs.a: The Edmonds School District. Five of its schools are inside the city: Mountlake Terrace High School, one middle school, and three elementary schools. Confirm your attendance area with the district before you advertise a school assignment.

faqs.q: Does the light rail station affect selling a Mountlake Terrace house?
faqs.a: It gives you a transit selling point. The Mountlake Terrace station has 890 parking stalls and has been served by Link light rail since the extension to Lynnwood opened in August 2024. Mention the station and the commute time when you describe the house.
